s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity edema with acute altered mental status and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Severe liver injury with elevated AST and ALT
Hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow
Extensive bilateral femoral-popliteal and iliac vein thrombosis
key_facts: 60-year-old man with hypertension and Parkinson’s disease
3 months of progressive lower extremity edema
Acute onset of altered mental status
Somnolent and disoriented on admission
Symmetric lower extremity edema on examination
Hepatomegaly and ascites without stigmata of chronic liver disease
AST 3877 U/L and ALT 2939 U/L
Total bilirubin 4.5 mg/dL and INR 3.8
White blood cell count 19.4×10^3/μL and platelets 63×10^3/μL
Lactic acid 13.9 mmol/L and BUN 67 mg/dL
Creatinine 3.3 mg/dL
Negative acetaminophen level and toxicology screen
Negative viral hepatitis panels, Epstein–Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and HIV testing
Diagnostic paracentesis negative for infection or malignancy
Hepatic ultrasonography with Doppler showed hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow

shortlist.label: Budd-Chiari syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow

shortlist.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Directly mentioned in key facts and supported by hepatic ultrasonography with Doppler

shortlist.label: Hepatorenal syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed hepatorenal syndrome requiring continuous venovenous hemofiltration

shortlist.label: Right atrial thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: Large echodense mass in the right atrium with preserved left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography

shortlist.label: Deep vein thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive bilateral femoral–popliteal and iliac vein thrombosis on lower-extremity Doppler ultrasonography

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with progressive lower extremity edema, hepatomegaly, ascites, and hepatic vein thrombosis with reversal of portal venous flow is consistent with Budd-Chiari syndrome, which is characterized by hepatic venous outflow obstruction.

rejected.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient has hepatic vein thrombosis, this is a key feature of Budd-Chiari syndrome, not a separate diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hepatorenal syndrome
rejected.why: The patient developed hepatorenal syndrome, but this is a complication of the underlying liver disease, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Right atrial thrombus
rejected.why: The patient has a right atrial thrombus, but this is likely a consequence of the hepatic vein thrombosis and Budd-Chiari syndrome.

rejected.label: Deep vein thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient has deep vein thrombosis, but this is not the primary diagnosis, and the hepatic vein thrombosis and Budd-Chiari syndrome are more significant findings.
